source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Recommend driving cessation solely because of chronological age without first assessing vision, cognition, motor function, or driving-related abilities.","B":"Assess driving-related vision, cognition, and motor/sensory function and discuss referral for a formal driving evaluation when specific concerns are identified.","C":"Ignore declining vision or slower reaction time because healthcare professionals have no role in counseling about driving-safety concerns.","D":"Treat one abnormal office measure as conclusive proof of unsafe driving without considering the broader functional assessment."}}
source_row.rationale: NHTSA guidance supports individualized assessment of driving-related vision, cognition and motor/sensory function, with referral or licensing review when indicated; chronological age alone is not an adequate determination of driving fitness.

source_row.stem: An older adult has declining vision and slower reaction time and asks whether age alone means driving must stop immediately. Which nursing approach is most appropriate?
